results.input: Làm thế nào để nấu món phở bò ngon?

result.actual_text:
Để nấu món phở bò ngon, bạn cần chuẩn bị các nguyên liệu và thực hiện theo các bước sau:

### Nguyên liệu:
1. **Nước dùng:**
   - Xương bò (xương ống hoặc xương đuôi)
   - Hành tây
   - Gừng
   - Gia vị: quế, hồi, đinh hương, tiêu, muối, đường

2. **Thịt bò:**
   - Thịt bò tái (thịt bò thăn hoặc bắp bò)
   - Thịt bò chín (nếu thích)

3. **Bánh phở:**
   - Bánh phở tươi hoặc khô

4. **Rau sống và gia vị:**
   - Húng quế, ngò gai, giá đỗ, chanh, ớt tươi, tương đen, tương ớt

### Cách làm:
1. **Nấu nước dùng:**
   - Rửa sạch xương bò, sau đó cho vào nồi nước sôi khoảng 5-10 phút để loại bỏ tạp chất. Sau đó, vớt xương ra và rửa lại.
   - Cho xương vào nồi lớn, thêm nước và đun sôi. Hạ lửa nhỏ và hầm trong khoảng 3-4 giờ để nước dùng ngọt và trong.
   - Nướng hành tây và gừng trên lửa cho đến khi có mùi thơm, sau đó cho vào nồi nước dùng cùng với các gia vị (quế, hồi, đinh hương, tiêu, muối, đường). Hầm thêm 1-2 giờ nữa.

2. **Chuẩn bị thịt bò:**
   - Thịt bò tái có thể thái mỏng và ướp với một chút muối và tiêu.
   - Nếu bạn muốn có thịt bò chín, có thể luộc hoặc hầm thịt bò cho đến khi chín mềm, sau đó thái lát.

3. **Nấu bánh phở:**
   - Nếu sử dụng bánh phở khô, hãy ngâm trong nước nóng cho mềm. Nếu sử dụng bánh phở tươi, chỉ cần trụng qua nước sôi.

4. **Hoàn thành món phở:**
   - Cho bánh phở vào bát, thêm thịt bò tái và thịt bò chín (nếu có).
   - Rót nước dùng nóng lên trên, trang trí với rau sống, húng quế, ngò gai, giá đỗ, chanh và ớt tươi.

5. **Thưởng thức:**
   - Dùng kèm với tương đen và tương ớt theo khẩu vị.

Chúc bạn thành công và có một bát phở bò ngon miệng!

items.title: Self-Driving Cars with Levelling Up Autonomy | IDTechEx Research Article
items.summary:
Jul 28, 2026 Lily-Rose Schuett

A car is driving itself down a road. 

Self-driving cars may have once been an imagined thing of the future, but with advancing technologies and systems, from radar to ADAS, autonomy is already levelling up, and level 3 vehicles and robotaxis can prove it. IDTechEx's portfolio of Robotics & Autonomy Research Reports and Subscriptions covers the latest developments within the autonomy for automotives sector.

ADAS and autonomy levels [...] Autonomous driving encompasses multiple technologies which all work alongside each other to create a wider system. These include a network of sensors, including radar and cameras, artificial intelligence, in-cabin monitoring, navigation and communication, and vehicle controls, each with their own roles to play in both vehicle autonomy and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). ADAS made an entrance when the first levels of autonomy came about, providing technologies to keep passengers safe [...] Robotaxis can allow for passengers to be transported around busy cities by driverless vehicles, showcasing the success of recent developments in robotics and autonomy globally.

items.title: Waymo's Self-Driving Cars Crash Less Often Than Human Drivers: Study
items.summary: Since Waymo arrived on the public stage as Google’s self-titled autonomous-driving project almost 20 years ago, the promise that self-driving cars would dramatically curtail crashes has remained just that. A handful of companies operate autonomous ride-hailing services in some cities (San Francisco is downright lousy with autonomous cars), but high-profile mishaps show how elusive real progress is. Yet Waymo may be heading in the right direction, according to the Insurance Institute for Highway [...] Researchers concluded that only 22% of the 736 autonomous-car crashes reported during the period studied were likely “police-reportable.” Of that total, 89 involved Waymo vehicles (the highest for a single operator), but only 64 of those were in autonomous mode. That’s not a very big dataset, and the complex process of getting to it shows how difficult it is to make any real conclusions about the safety of self-driving cars. [...] But as the IIHS explains in an accompanying press release, getting any meaningful comparison between human and autonomous driving wasn’t easy. While companies are required to report crashes involving self-driving cars to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and the State of California, they aren’t required to report the mileage these vehicles cover, or how much is actually done in autonomous mode. That makes it impossible to know how common self-driving car crashes really

items.title: How San Diego helped launch the self-driving car era
items.summary:
The big picture: This minivan was one of the first demonstrations that self-driving cars were possible. It helped pave the way for some of the autonomous vehicles we see today, Todd Jochem, who worked on the project, told Axios.

Driving the news: Thursday was the 31st anniversary of that drive.

   Jochem has written a book about it, called "Driven."

Along with finishing the drive in San Diego, the city played another key part in driverless history. [...] Two years later, Jochem and a team from Carnegie Mellon used the HOV lanes on I-15 to run "Demo '97," a demonstration that showed fully autonomous cars and buses driving in realistic traffic scenarios.

Fast forward: The technology for driverless cars on highways was 90% of the way there in 1997, Jochem told Axios.
